title: Finite-stage smooth dualizing complex
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $a_X:X\to s$ be separated, of finite type, and smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\omega_X=Ra_X^!A_s$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. The canonical smooth purity isomorphism of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], at $f=a_X$ and $K=A_s$, gives an isomorphism
$$
 \eta_X:\omega_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d],
$$
where the twist is [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. More precisely, $\eta_X^{-1}$ is $\gamma_{a_X,A_s}$ after the canonical identification $La_X^*A_s\cong A_X$.

Let $\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}:Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A_s$ be the counit. Then
$$
 \varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}\circ Ra_{X!}(\eta_X^{-1})
 =\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,A_s}:
 Ra_{X!}(A_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow A_s,
$$
the smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. After evaluation at the geometric point of $s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], this is the integration map
$$
 R\Gamma_c(X,A_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow A.
$$
Its normalization is the affine-space normalization of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity]: for the structural projection $p_d:\mathbf A_k^d\to s$, this map sends the ordered fundamental class of $\mathbf A_k^d$, the $d$-fold tensor of the normalized affine-line classes, to $1\in A$.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $B=A_s$. The object $B$ in degree zero belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$: its only cohomology sheaf is the constant finite free rank-one $A$-module, so the single stratum $s$ witnesses constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and $B\otimes_A^L M=M$ for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $M$, so its Tor interval is $[0,0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The identity is computed by the free rank-one complex itself, with no higher terms. The conventions [def-pur-conventions] define $\omega_X=Ra_X^!B$ and supply the constructible exceptional adjunction for this separated finite-type structure map. The schemes $X$ and $s$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and the stated smoothness has pure relative dimension $d$, so all geometric hypotheses of finite-coefficient smooth purity hold.

source.place: First sentence: verify the coefficient object and all hypotheses before applying purity

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] to $f=a_X$ and $K=B$, whose hypotheses were checked in Step 1. It gives an isomorphism $\gamma_{a_X,B}:La_X^*B(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_X$. The statement of [def-pur-smooth-trace] explicitly includes the canonical identification $La_X^*B\cong A_X$ at finite coefficients. Write $u:La_X^*B(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$ for this identification with the same twist and shift. Set $c=\gamma_{a_X,B}\circ u^{-1}$ and $\eta_X=u\circ\gamma_{a_X,B}^{-1}$. Then $\eta_Xc=1$ and $c\eta_X=1$ by cancellation, so $\eta_X$ is exactly the claimed canonical identification and $c=\eta_X^{-1}$.

source.place: First sentence: specialize purity and invert it in the stated direction

proof.text: Let $F=Ra_{X!}$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{a_X,B}$. By the displayed defining composite in [def-pur-smooth-trace], read through its included unit identification, $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,B}=\varepsilon\circ F(c)$. Since $c=\eta_X^{-1}$, this is precisely the counit expressed on $F(A_X(d)[2d])$. Explicitly, $F(\eta_X)F(c)=F(1)=1$ and $F(c)F(\eta_X)=1$, so the change of source is the specified one, with no choice of a scalar. The same definition states that this trace is a morphism between bounded constructible objects, so geometric-point evaluation is defined. Apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$, which at finite level is evaluation of complexes at the point [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. It sends $B$ to $A$ and, by the defining formula of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], sends $F(A_X(d)[2d])$ to $R\Gamma_c(X,A_X(d)[2d])$. Functoriality carries the displayed equality of maps to the asserted integration map of $A$-complexes.

source.place: Second sentence: expand the defining smooth trace and apply point evaluation

proof.text: For the normalization, specialize the affine-space clause of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] to $\Lambda=A$ and $p_d:\mathbf A_k^d\to s$. Its source and target are exactly the integration source and target of Step 3 for $X=\mathbf A_k^d$. That clause says that the smooth trace is the product of the normalized affine-line traces and sends their ordered $d$-fold fundamental class to $1$. This proves the claimed normalization in the precise model where the cited theorem states it. In particular, the normalization used here is the one fixed by the affine-line/diagonal-purity route, with no replacement of its purity map.

source.place: Last sentence: use exactly the cited affine-space normalization clause

blueprint_update.statement:
Work in the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], let
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type,
smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The dualizing complex

$$
\omega_X=Ra_X^!A
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_X\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A_X(d)[2d],
$$

coming from [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], and the counit
$Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A$ is the normalized integration map

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,A_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow A
$$

of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity], sending the
fundamental class of the $d$-dimensional oriented fiber to $1$.

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] to $f=a_X$ and
$K=A$: its source $La_X^*A(d)[2d]$ is $A_X(d)[2d]$, giving the
identification of the dualizing complex. Under this identification the
counit $Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!A\to A$ is, by [def-pur-smooth-trace], the
smooth trace
$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,A}$, whose normalization is
[thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] in the case
$Y=\Spec k$.

The hypotheses of thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity (smooth, separated, pure relative dimension d, separated finite-type k-schemes) hold. Step 2: gamma and the unit identification La^*Lambda_Y = Lambda_X stated in def-pur-smooth-trace give eta = u o gamma^{-1} with the correct directions. Step 3: by def-pur-smooth-trace, the counit composed with Ra_!(eta^{-1}) is the smooth trace, its K=Lambda_Y case being the first composite. Fib_s (def-weil-finite-coefficient-point item 1) and RGamma_c = Fib_s Ra_! (def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology) are applied to objects that def-pur-smooth-trace puts in D^b_c. Step 4: the affine-space clause of thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity is used verbatim at Lambda=A; checked at d=0 and d=1. The STATEMENT-DISPUTED correction is justified: for X = two copies of Spec k and d=0 the class (1,1) integrates to 2, and empty X has no class. The replacement is exactly what the cited theorem states, with no hypothesis added and the purity isomorphism and counit identification kept for all X.
